chapter: New Orleans style and bass playing
title: European and revival bands learning from records
summary: Garland says players like Clancy Hayes and Europeans learned from Ory and Oliver records, and agrees there is a New Orleans style.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: All right, okay. One question was, you know, you read in all the jazz books and you hear people talking about the New Orleans style and so then we heard all of the traditional stuff in Europe, the Trad stuff as they call it and the revival stuff, mostly by white bands, who studied the old recordings and so on, and I wonder if they helped people know what the New Orleans music was or they got in the way of it. For example, Clancy Hayes and the banjo and all that singing, you know, Turk, and all that stuff or was
Well, Clancy got all that stuff, you know, from the records, you know, of Kid Ory, King Oliver, those bands, you understand. And they passed it around, you understand?
Just like the boys over in Europe, they take those records and they play those numbers off the record, they learn them off the record, and then they play them almost as good as the original band.
And they're pretty good at it.
Would you say, then, is there a real -- then is there a New Orleans style?
Okay, then we could talk about that?
Good, okay. So that'll be one, that'll be a question, okay?
